subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: According to collision theory, for a reaction to occur, particles must collide with a certain minimum energy and:
questions.explain: Collision theory states that reactions happen only when particles collide with sufficient energy and in the correct orientation.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT increase the rate of a chemical reaction?
questions.explain: Lowering the temperature reduces particle energy and collision frequency, so it slows the reaction down.

questions.q: Why does increasing the temperature increase the rate of a reaction?
options: Particles move faster, so they collide more frequently and more have the activation energy
Particles become larger and collide more easily
The activation energy of the reaction is lowered
The concentration of the reactants increases
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, increasing both collision frequency and the proportion of successful collisions.

questions.q: Increasing the concentration of a reactant in solution increases the rate of reaction because:
options: there are more particles in a given volume, so collisions are more frequent
the particles have more energy per collision
questions.explain: A higher concentration packs more particles into the same volume, so collisions happen more often.

questions.q: A catalyst is a substance that:
options: speeds up a reaction without being used up itself
is always used up during the reaction
increases the temperature of the reaction
changes the amount of product formed
questions.explain: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction but is not consumed and can be reused.

questions.q: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
It increases the kinetic energy of the particles
It raises the temperature of the reaction mixture
It increases the concentration of the reactants
questions.explain: A catalyst lowers the activation energy by offering a different reaction pathway, so more collisions are successful.

questions.q: Breaking a solid reactant into smaller pieces increases the rate of reaction because it:
options: increases the surface area exposed to the other reactant
increases the temperature of the solid
increases the concentration of the solid
questions.explain: Smaller pieces have a larger surface area to volume ratio, exposing more particles for collisions.

questions.q: The activation energy of a reaction is:
options: the minimum energy particles must have to react on collision
the energy released when a reaction takes place
the total energy of the reactants
the energy stored in the products
questions.explain: Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need for a successful reaction.

questions.q: In an experiment, 30 cm3 of gas is produced in 60 seconds. What is the mean rate of reaction?
questions.explain: Mean rate = quantity of product / time = 30 cm3 / 60 s = 0.5 cm3/s.

questions.q: Which method is suitable for measuring the rate of a reaction that produces a gas?
options: Measuring the volume of gas collected over time
Measuring the colour of the solution
Measuring the mass of the beaker
Measuring the pH of the solution
questions.explain: The volume of gas released can be measured over time using a gas syringe to follow the rate.

questions.q: Which symbol is used to represent a reversible reaction?
questions.explain: The double half-arrow ⇌ shows that a reaction can proceed in both the forward and backward directions.

questions.q: In a reversible reaction at dynamic equilibrium in a closed system:
options: the forward and backward reactions occur at the same rate
only the forward reaction is occurring
the concentrations of reactants and products are always equal
questions.explain: At dynamic equilibrium the forward and backward reactions happen at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.q: For an exothermic forward reaction at equilibrium, increasing the temperature will:
options: shift the equilibrium towards the reactants, reducing yield
shift the equilibrium towards the products, increasing yield
have no effect on the position of equilibrium
questions.explain: Increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium in the endothermic (backward) direction, reducing the yield of products for an exothermic forward reaction.

questions.q: For a gaseous equilibrium, increasing the pressure shifts the position of equilibrium towards:
options: the side with fewer molecules of gas
the side with more molecules of gas
questions.explain: Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules, which reduces the pressure again.

questions.q: A reversible reaction has an endothermic forward direction. To increase the yield of product, you should:
questions.explain: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic forward direction, increasing the yield of product.

questions.q: The standard unit used to express the concentration of a solution in this topic is:
questions.explain: Concentration is commonly expressed in moles per cubic decimetre (mol/dm3), and also in g/dm3.

questions.q: During an acid-alkali titration, which piece of apparatus is used to add the acid a small amount at a time?
questions.explain: A burette delivers accurately measured, variable volumes of solution during a titration.

questions.q: In a titration, an indicator is used to:
options: show the end point where the reaction is just complete
increase the concentration of the acid
questions.explain: An indicator changes colour at the end point, showing when the acid and alkali have exactly reacted.

questions.q: What is the concentration of a solution containing 0.5 mol of solute dissolved in 250 cm3 of solution?
questions.explain: Concentration = moles / volume = 0.5 mol / 0.25 dm3 = 2 mol/dm3.

questions.q: How many moles of HCl are present in 25 cm3 of hydrochloric acid with a concentration of 0.2 mol/dm3?
questions.explain: Moles = concentration × volume = 0.2 mol/dm3 × 0.025 dm3 = 0.005 mol.
